title: Prompt-enhancement settings - the DeepInfra key, the Ollama models, and which LLM enhances

summary: plan.md written: 3 phases. Planning pass resized the card against disk - the DeepInfra key STORE already exists (main/secretsStore.js + js/core/secretsClient.js + bridge + tests), so gap 1 is a UI field only; the deletion and the picker are ONE edit because chooseEngineModelId() dies without a preference to return; and the test surface is three whole test functions, not the four assertions the card names. One decision left open for Fabio: whether the in-graph comfy backend becomes pick-only.

Fabio redesigned it mid-conversation: one dropdown per JOB, each listing BACKENDS (DeepInfra/Ollama/ComfyUI) not model ids, framed as compute PLACEMENT not model quality. My open question was dissolved by a measurement - both standalone graphs carry their own CLIPLoader, so the four-model ComfyUI gate is VRAM-thrift, not capability. Phase 1 gained the chooseBackend:153 fix (it silently downgrades an explicit comfy pick to ollama) and a verify-on-a-non-Krea-model precondition.

note: Checklist derived from the three plan phases at todo -> doing.

Precondition PASSED: the standalone qwen3vl enhancer graph ran on the bench (8188) with no generation model loaded - 15s, prompt_id 7af9b68e, subject kept. CLIPLoader type "krea2" is a CLIP-type string, not a model dependency. "ComfyUI on every model" stands.

Price in the picker built (Fabio chose A): live DeepInfra per-1M prices on cloud model options plus a billing note. npm test 949/949, lint clean, live fetch and route smoke pass. Desktop check pending.

Round 4: Fabio saw the price lines in the app. DeepSeek V3.2 and Qwen 3.6 35B deleted from MODEL_REGISTRY as overkill for enhancement (no docs/scripts/tests referenced them). npm test 949/949, lint clean, route returns 4 models with the two Gemmas priced. Descriptions via DeepInfra vision confirmed as MPI-737 scope.
Round 4 verified by Fabio in the app ("1"): DeepInfra prices in the picker, cloud list trimmed to the two Gemmas, billing note. Next: phase 3, the Ollama lifecycle, in a fresh session.
